criteria.criterion: The root cause of the false 'does not follow from job X's records' for an intervention re-score in a squash is identified in code comments or the commit message, citing the differing field(s).
criteria.evidence: The new comment in jobs.rs expected_score explains that a squash puts the closing score and its later interventions in one tree. Recomputing from the whole tree resolves `user_intervenes` to true too early, so the score differs in `events[user_intervenes].outcome`, `.provisional` and `.brier`. CHANGELOG and decision D71 give the same cause. D71 also names the first differing field the tests hit: `events[2].brier.reader`.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs no longer reports a re-score as not following from the records when the squash tree holds the closing score, the intervention and its re-score for the same job, as `athena intervene --job` writes them.
criteria.evidence: expected_score now keeps only interventions with `i.at <= at`. I read score_records and rescore in athena-score/src/lib.rs. The closing score (made at T, before the intervention) is now recomputed without the later intervention, so `user_intervenes` stays false and provisional, matching what was written. The re-score's `at` is after its intervention's `at`, because manage.rs calls now() for the intervention first. So the intervention is counted, and rescore() then resolves the event the same way `athena intervene` did (manage.rs:328 calls rescore on the latest score).

criteria.criterion: A new test builds a squash (chain or single job) containing a landed job plus an intervention and its re-score, and asserts check() returns no violations. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
criteria.evidence: The new test landing_tests::a_squash_with_an_intervention_and_its_rescore_lands builds a squash commit with a landed job, its closing score, an intervention and its re-score. It asserts that judge plus job_records_of return no violations. It passed, and all 69 athena-gate tests passed. I did not revert the fix to watch the test fail. Reasoning from score_records: without the filter, the closing score is recomputed with intervened=true and differs, so the test would fail, as D71 says.

criteria.criterion: The existing test hand_written_scores_and_outcomes_are_refused still passes: a forged perfect re-score (all Brier values zeroed) with a real intervention is still refused with 'does not follow'. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle hand_written`.
criteria.evidence: hand_written_scores_and_outcomes_are_refused passed (2 passed, 0 failed). A new gate test, a_squash_with_a_forged_rescore_is_still_refused, also checks that zeroed Brier values in a squash are refused with 'does not follow'. It passed.

criteria.criterion: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.
criteria.evidence: fmt and clippy finished with no output and no errors. cargo test --locked: every suite reported ok with 0 failed; only the live-model tests were ignored.

findings.summary: The new test builds its 'recorded' closing score with expected_score itself, not through athena's real closing path, so the check is partly circular.
findings.evidence: `let closing = crate::jobs::expected_score(&git, &landed_tree, ...)` is computed on the tree before the intervention is added. This does copy how the real closing score is made, before any later intervention. But the CLI's real closing-score writer is never compared against the gate's recomputation.

findings.summary: The reported failure was not reproduced on the two jobs named in the request, or on the simulated PR #9 squash.
findings.evidence: D71 says: "The two job ids named in the request were not examined." The cause was reproduced only with a synthetic test, although the reading asked the producer to reproduce the failure first.

summary: The change passes. The history check wrongly refused job scores in a squash because it rebuilt each score using every intervention in the final tree, including ones made after the score was written. That flipped the `user_intervenes` event's outcome, provisional flag and Brier values. The fix is a one-line filter in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs: count only interventions made at or before the score's own time. I read the scoring and `athena intervene` code: closing scores now match the records, and re-scores still match what `athena intervene --job` writes. Forged re-scores are still refused, by both a new gate test and the existing lifecycle test. I ran `cargo test -p athena-gate`, the `hand_written` lifecycle test, fmt, clippy and the full test suite; all passed. Two minor gaps. First, the new test builds the recorded closing score with the checker's own function rather than athena's real closing path. Second, the fix was not tried on the two jobs named in the request or on the simulated PR #9 squash, so whether those two now pass is unconfirmed.
